default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-168.title: Post-settlement drift fade
E-168.hypothesis: WIN's daily settlement price is set from the 17:00-17:15 window; after it, the cash market is closed and index arbitrage is gone, so a futures-only drift away from the settlement-window average is thin speculative flow that dealers lean against (they hedge at tomorrow's cash open); fade a stretch from that average on the first bar closing back toward it.

E-169.title: Indecision cluster at an extreme, break against
E-169.hypothesis: Several normal-size small-body bars sitting at the high of the last hour show buyers and sellers trading two-way at the top with no buyer paying up; when price then closes below the cluster's low, the buyers who stood in the cluster are trapped and the push is over, so sell (mirror at the low).

E-170.title: Dollar-priced index break follow
E-170.hypothesis: Foreign investors, the marginal Ibovespa buyers, watch the index in dollars (WIN / WDO); a new window high of that ratio while WIN in reais is still under its own window high means foreign holders already see a breakout and their stops/entries trigger, which then lifts WIN; follow it (mirror).

E-171.title: Heavy-churn session edge fade
E-171.hypothesis: A session trading far more contracts than usual for the minute while its range is no wider than usual is dominated by two-sided size (hedgers, arbitrage, market makers) absorbing both directions; in that regime a bar that pokes to a new short-term extreme but closes against its open meets that absorption, so fade it.

E-172.title: Failed VWAP-band reversion follow
E-172.hypothesis: A stretch from the session VWAP draws mean-reversion traders; when price reverts toward VWAP and then stretches out beyond the band again, the faders of the first stretch are trapped a second time and their stops plus the trend side's adds carry the move; follow the second exit from the band (mirror).

E-173.title: Failed-breakout high re-break follow
E-173.hypothesis: A poke above the recent high that closes back inside invites fade traders who put their stops just above the poke's high; a later close above that failure high within the next minutes runs those stops and shows the breakout side has absorbed the faders, so follow it (mirror at lows).

E-174.title: Alternating-tape end follow
E-174.hypothesis: A run of closes that flip sign every bar is quote bouncing by liquidity providers with no initiator; two same-sign closes in a row that also clear the alternating zone's high mark the first initiative order breaking the bounce, and makers pull quotes in its direction; follow it (mirror).

E-175.title: Overnight dollar-gap index catch-down
E-175.hypothesis: An opening dollar gap well above normal is overnight risk-off news priced by FX dealers; when WIN opened without pricing at least half of it, foreign equity desks sell the index during the morning to catch up, so sell WIN counter bars (close below the prior low) early in the session (mirror for a dollar gap down).

E-176.title: London-close move fade
E-176.hypothesis: European desks that trade Brazilian exposure flatten into the London close (12:30 or 13:30 in Sao Paulo, by season); a WIN hour that moved much more than usual into that time carried their closing flow, which then stops, so in the following hour fade the move on the first bar closing back past the prior bar.

E-177.title: Absorbed heavy counter bar in a session trend
E-177.hypothesis: In a session trend (price on the rising side of a rising VWAP), a counter bar on heavy volume is a large seller hitting bids; when the very next bar closes above that bar's high, the trend side absorbed the whole sale and the seller is under water at once, so the trend resumes; follow it (mirror).
